newsitem.title: NORWAY: Norway's Hydro profits fall in first half.
newsitem.headline: Norway's Hydro profits fall in first half.

text.p: Norway's largest public company, Norsk Hydro, said Monday that first-half 1997 pretax profits fell 4.5 percent despite higher operating income as retail gasoline sales and fertiliser margins slid and expenses rose.

The industrial giant booked profits before tax for the first six months of 5.87 billion crowns ($795 million), vs. 6.14 billion ($827.5 million) in the corresponding 1996 period. Operating profits grew 4 percent to 5.98 billion crowns ($806 million) from 5.75 billion crowns ($775 million).

Net financial charges surged to 405 million ($54.6 million), compared with an income of 61 million crowns ($8.2 million). Earnings per share fell to 13.30 crowns ($1.79) from 14.40 crowns ($1.94) for the first half 1996.
Hydro attributed the improvement in operating income to higher earnings for oil and gas, light metals and petrochemicals. Agriculture earnings declined, it said.

"The work to realise the growth strategies presented last year is on schedule and investments in the first half of the year totalled 5.7 billion crowns ($768.2 billion)," Hydro President Egil Myklebust said in a statement.
"Several divisions have put into effect initiatives aimed at reducing costs, while other cost-reduction programmes are about to be introduced."

An Oslo-based analyst said Hydro results was not great but it wasn't a disaster, either. "We knew fertiliser prices had been dropping this year, so really we should have seen this coming. But the rest of the year could be tricky," he said.
